slot.brief: Magnetic moment of a given transition-metal ion: write d configuration and count unpaired electrons / compute √n(n+2)

stem: The spin-only magnetic moment of $\text{Cr}^{3+}$ is closest to which value?

verdicts.working: Cr³⁺ has a 3d³ configuration, with 3 unpaired electrons. The spin-only moment is √[3(3+2)] = √15 ≈ 3.87 BM.

working:
$\text{Cr}^{3+}:[\text{Ar}]3d^3$; $n=3$.
$\mu=\sqrt{n(n+2)}=\sqrt{3(5)}=\sqrt{15}=3.87\ \text{BM}$

Independent check: Cr³⁺ has a 3d³ configuration, with 3 unpaired electrons. The spin-only moment is √[3(3+2)] = √15 ≈ 3.87 BM.
solution:
For $\text{Cr}^{3+}$, the configuration is $[\text{Ar}]3d^3$, giving $n=3$ unpaired electrons.
$$\mu=\sqrt{n(n+2)}=\sqrt{3(5)}=\sqrt{15}\approx 3.87\ \text{BM}$$
